messages:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Pager: Elevated 5xxs observed for /v1/paging and /v1/console-request endpoints — aggregated error rate 8.5% (5m) — affected regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1. Paging SLA impact likely. Correlation ids: range 7f2..7fa. Paging routing shows mismatch between console and control plane configs. Paging runbook pinged.

maria: I’m on it. Just pulled the initial metrics. Dataplane token logs show many `INVALID_ROUTE` spikes at the same minutes where console UI shows requests succeeding. Looks like console is hitting cached routes.

ken: @maria — can you post a small timeline? when did the first spike start? any recent config pushes?

maria: First spike at 1865431980 (≈3.5m ago). We had a config rollout at 1865429500 this morning for feature flag `paging_v2_routing` (rollout 30%). Canaryed in control plane only earlier this week. No automatic gate for dataplane propagation in that deploy.

samir: I see an internal flag flip for `paging_v2_routing` in the control plane API logs at 1865429487. But the dataplane agents show no corresponding config update — they still report `routing_version: v1`.

opsbot: command run by tess: `rdwctl configs get --scope=dataplane --service=paging --since=1865429000`

```
# output
- node-a: routing_version: v1
- node-b: routing_version: v1
- node-c: unreachable (timeout)
```

eli: node-c being unreachable is concerning. Could be transient comms or a controlplane push failure. Any obvious network flaps?

tess: Checked infra metrics — no network alerts. But there was a control-plane db migration 1865429400 that had a brief primaries switchover (db-primary->db-primary-2). That might have caused the config distributor to miss a few pushes.

maria: Hypothesis 1: control plane updated the routing flag, console reads the new flag (since console hits the control plane API directly), but the config distributor failed to push to dataplane nodes during the DB switchover window. Result: console shows new routes, dataplane still serving v1 routes -> mismatched behavior and 5xxs when console-annotated requests are routed to nodes without route entries.

ken: Good hypothesis. For mitigation we can: 1) force re-push of current config to all dataplane nodes (non-disruptive), 2) toggle console to fallback mode so it uses legacy routing for now, or 3) temporarily route paging traffic to dedicated fallback pool (if capacity exists). Which do we want to do first?

samir: I can run the re-push. Will use `rdwctl configs push --target=dataplane --service=paging --force --trace` and watch for ack. Planning to start now. Posting trace link: https://logs.internal/trace/7f2abc (redacted)

opsbot: samir started configs push at 1865432165 — tracking acks.

maria: Also paging customer-impact notes: several large customers reported failed live handoffs and latency spikes in the console — CS has been paged. @customer-sre are you with us?

customer-sre: here — we’re fielding a couple of tickets. Customers seeing 503s on cancellation/handshake flows. We’ve advised temporary retry/backoff. Please update ASAP so we can inform customers.

samir: Push progress: node-a ack 1865432190, node-b ack 1865432202, node-c still unreachable. Getting `handshake timeout` to distributor from node-c.

eli: node-c’s logs: `2024-07-21T10:22:30Z distributor: push: handshake failed: EOF` and `2024-07-21T10:22:31Z network: conn reset by peer`. Looks like the agent flapped. Ops infra, can you check node-c host health?

tess: infra check: host node-c (ip 10.4.33.21) has high cpu (95%) and kube oomkill events at 1865432005. Recent container restart for `dataplane-agent`. I’ll spin it into maintenance and attempt a restart.

opsbot: maintenance scheduled for node-c by tess at 1865432230.

ken: While we restart node-c, we should enable console fallback to reduce customer impact. Maria, can you flip console to `legacy_routing_mode=true` for the UI layer? That’s a quick toggle (no deploy).

maria: Doing it now: `rdwctl feature flip --service=console --flag=legacy_routing_mode --set=true --actor=maria`

opsbot: command result: flag set. Console reads will now prefer legacy routing for new requests for up to 60s due to client caches.

maria: Confirmed observed drop in error rate to ~2.1% after console fallback starting 1865432250. Customer-sre: please verify if the in-flight tickets are moving to success with retries.

customer-sre: early reports look good, some customers see restored flows after retries. We’ll hold comms until you confirm full mitigation.

samir: node-c handled restart and rejoin at 1865432325. Re-push acks all returned by 1865432330. Distributor logs show full config sync.

opsbot: configs push completed at 1865432330 — all dataplane nodes now report `routing_version: v2`.

eli: Can confirm dataplane logs now accept routes for v2 and 5xxs are trending down. Need to verify no lingering drift between console and control plane snapshots.

maria: Good. Next steps for in-incident RCA: 1) build a timeline with exact DB switchover window and push attempts, 2) collect distributor logs and agent logs for node-c, 3) correlate client traces for correlation ids 7f2..7fa, 4) draft mitigation blameless note for customers.

ken: I’ll take timeline assembly. samir, please upload `rdwctl push --trace` log and distributor logs to the incident bucket with path: `gs://incidents/1865432100/` and post links here.

samir: Uploaded: https://gs.internal/incidents/1865432100/distributor.log and https://gs.internal/incidents/1865432100/push-trace.log

maria: I’ll own the immediate RCA writeup. ken will stitch timeline. tess — can you add a short infra action: ensure distributor push has retry logic across DB primary switchover windows. If not, add ticket.

tess: Filed INFRA-4892: `distributor: resilient re-push across db-primary switchover` — assigning to infra team.

opsbot: Oncall handoff reminder: @ken will be primary for the next 30 minutes for further mitigation followups.

ken: I’ll take handoff. Leaving this thread with pinned notes: mitigation applied (console fallback toggled, config re-pushed, node-c restarted), customer impact reduced, artifacts uploaded. Will convene a brief post-incident sync at +2h for final RCA comments.

maria: Thanks all. Closing live mitigation. Please add any conflicting hypotheses here if you have them.

eli: Alternate hypothesis: token-cache mismatch causing some requests to validate against stale ACLs — logs don’t show that yet but will include it in timeline checks.

samir: Noted. I’ll grep for ACL errors in agent logs.

maria: End of thread — we’ll convert this into a formal incident RCA doc with timeline and customer-facing blameless note.
